newsitem.title: INDIA: India Sterlite shares up on smelter news.
newsitem.headline: India Sterlite shares up on smelter news.

text.p: Shares of Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd gained 10.75 rupees, or 4.69 percent, to 240.0 at the Bombay exchange on Wednesday after the firm said it expected a state government decision this week on reopening its smelter plant, traders said.
"We hope to get the direction (from the government) in a day or two," K. Ranganathan, general manager (commercial) of Sterlite Industries, told Reuters by telephone on Tuesday.

Earlier this month the Tamil Nadu government asked Sterlite to shut down operations at its copper smelter at the southern port of Tuticorin after it was suspected of gas emissions that sent more than 100 workers in a nearby factory to hospital.
The company strongly denies there was any gas leakage.
"There was no leakage of any kind from our plant," it said in a statement.
Tarun Jain, a senior Sterlite official, told Reuters the expert panel set up by the state government to examine the suspected leak had submitted its report last week.
"We hope that the committee will take the same view as us," Jain said.
The smelter, with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes, began operations in December 1996.
Sterlite officials said the closure was costing the company 25 million rupees ($700,280) daily.
